# Pilot C notebooks (run on Kaggle; generated by `build_notebooks.py`)

Each notebook is self-contained: the repo code (`common/`, `pilot_c/`) is inlined as `%%writefile`
cells. Regenerate after any code change: `python notebooks/build_notebooks.py`.

| Notebook | Accelerator | Quota | What it does | Output to commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pilot_c_gold_check_cpu/` | None (CPU) | 0 GPU h | Applies each task's gold patch in the scorer's verification path; tells us which tasks are solvable at all on Kaggle | `pilot_c_gold_check_kaggle.json` |
| `pilot_c_smoke_timing/` | GPU L4 x4 | ≈1.2–1.75 L4x4 h (hard stop 1.75 h) | 3 tasks × {e4b, e2b, 12b, 31b} at O0, plus e4b at O-all | `pilot_c_smoke_timing.json` |
| `pilot_c_pilot_e4b/` | GPU L4 x4 | estimate after smoke (hard stop 3.9 h) | e4b × 15 tasks × {O0, O-func, O-all, O0 again} | `pilot_c_pilot_e4b.json` |

How to run (UI): New Notebook → File → Import notebook (the `.ipynb`) → Add inputs: competition
`gemma-4-developer-agent`, dataset `metric/gemma-4-developer-agent-wheelhouse`, and for the GPU
notebooks the Gemma 4 QAT models (`google/gemma-4`, Other: e4b, e2b, 12b, 31b `-it-qat-w4a16-ct`, version 2)
→ Settings: accelerator as in the table, internet off → Save Version → "Save & Run All".
Environment: the metadata pins the same docker image as the official starter; in the UI use
"Pin to original environment" if offered, so library versions match the starter.

CLI alternative: put your username in `kernel-metadata.json` (`id`), then
`kaggle kernels push -p notebooks/pilot_c_<name>`.

Data rule: everything the notebooks write under `/kaggle/working/private/` (hinted task copies,
gold locations, patches, traces) is competition-derived. Leave it on Kaggle. Commit only the
`pilot_c_*.json` files (numbers and task IDs only) into `results/`.
